name: Anthology Fund
identity_check: The Anthology Fund, a $100M early-stage AI initiative announced 2024-07-17 by Menlo Ventures in partnership with Anthropic; it is run by Menlo partners and lives on menlovc.com/anthology-fund. Not Anthology Inc. (education software) or Anthology Development. Anthropic's announcement says it is financed by Menlo, so type is vc, not cvc.

pages.title: Anthropic partners with Menlo Ventures to launch Anthology Fund
Q2 2025 Update from the Anthology Fund
BeHeard Announced As One of 18 Startups for Anthology Fund and New Financing

type.snippet: financed by Menlo to support startups innovating broadly with Anthropic technology

stages.snippet: We will make Pre-Seed, Seed, and Series A investments

thesis_text.value: Backs AI founders building on or aligned with Anthropic technology, spanning infrastructure, applications, consumer AI, trust and safety, and societal benefit.

stated_sectors.snippet: novel applications of AI in industries like healthcare, education, scientific research, and more

rounds.snippet: included participation from True Ventures, Ridge Ventures and Sterling Road

conflicts.reason: The FAQ is the more specific statement of what the fund actually does; the page body is marketing copy.
Menlo's pages disagree; the later Q2 2025 update says $30K Anthropic credits plus $100K AWS credits.

open_items: Only one round recorded. Goodfire (Series A $50M, 2025-04-17, led by Menlo) is described by Menlo as having been backed at seed by the Anthology Fund, but the Series A page does not name the Anthology Fund in that round; seed amount and date not found. Other cohort names (Mercor, All Hands, Crosswise, Accordance, Brellium, New Lantern, Alma, Astrix) come from a Pulse 2.0 cohort list with no round details.

HQ not recorded: no fetched page states a location for the fund (Menlo Ventures' own location not verified here). Close date is the announcement date; a 'close' is not a concept for this rolling initiative.
The Menlo FAQ says terms are negotiated case by case; leads are described as seven- to 10-year commitments. Per Menlo's Q2 2025 update, over 30 Anthology companies by August 2025.
Fund-mgmt: investment team named on the Menlo page includes Menlo partners; partners not recorded for Tier B.
